summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). Thermal Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed=false, and no artifacts were produced. The selected scenario is Figure 15 of W2888269620, comparing four-layer, 64-core PTO TSV and PTM M3D small-world NoCs with static VFI, using HotSpot and GEM5/McPAT. The experiment is typed custom_2d_steady, so even if it had run it would be steady-only with no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes or powers were used, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated and no source commit or placement assumption applies. The extraction contains an empty floorplan and an empty power_w, so a custom experiment with 1-128 blocks and a power object could not be formed. Blocking facts also include an evidence item with no valid page or asset locator, no cited thermal observable or steady/transient regime, and unresolved adversarial code, parameters, config and data checks plus a pending independent page/asset review. The deterministic gate sets comparison_valid=false, so there is no numerical comparison with the paper. The paper's reported values (peak temperature up to 29.1% lower for M3D, average 20.1%, mean max-min spread 16.7 C TSV vs 2.9 C M3D, 110 C throttle limit not triggered) are context only. Those values are an aggregation over benchmarks of a 3D four-tier HotSpot result with unpublished boundary conditions, and no matching 2D location, aggregation, regime or boundary assumption exists. Qualitatively, the paper attributes the M3D advantage to lower inter-tier thermal resistance (thin ILD with MIVs vs TSV with bonding layers), which a single-layer 2D steady model cannot capture. No exact replication is claimed and the final verdict stays not_2d_applicable.

The paper models a 4-tier 3D stack (TSV with BCB bonding layers versus monolithic ILD with MIVs), which a 2D steady-state Studio runner cannot represent, so inter-tier thermal resistance and the TSV/M3D difference are lost.

The M3D versus TSV result depends on vertical thermal resistance (R_j, R_b) and layer material differences extracted from HotSpot. These parameters are not published in the paper, so they cannot be reproduced.

The study is a multi-core NoC (cores, routers, links, VFI clusters) with architecture-level placement optimization. The paper publishes no per-block geometry, coordinates or power values, so no complete floorplan or power table exists.

The optimizer is simulated annealing over NoC core, router and link placement with a joint performance-temperature cost, while a Studio thermal runner would use a different or no optimizer. The optimizer is therefore not replicated.
The workload power comes from GEM5/McPAT per benchmark with static VFI voltage-frequency levels. These powers are not published, and no controller or time series is available.

The cooling and heat-sink boundary conditions, package and interposer model are not specified in the paper, though the heat sink location is described qualitatively (high-power VFI clusters near the sink).

No transient behavior, reliability analysis (e.g., NBTI, mentioned only qualitatively) or throttling dynamics are simulated. The paper reports steady-style max/avg/min temperatures with no throttling triggered.
